title: Taranga 7. The Spreading of the Books of Bhakti
html:
Srinivasa, Narottama and Shyamananda journey to Gauda with the books; the books are stolen near Vishnupura; Srinivasa with King Vira Hambira: the reading of the Bhagavatam, the recovery of the books, mercy to the king; news sent to Vrindavana; accounts of the Lord's associates; Shrikhanda and Kantaka-nagara

1Glory, glory to Sri Krishna Chaitanya, the friend of the lowly!
Glory, glory to Nityananda, the ocean of compassion!

2Glory to Sri Advaita-deva, the abode of virtues!
Glory to Sri Gadadhara Pandita, full of prema!

3Glory to Srivasa Pandita, the giver of prema-bhakti!
Glory to Vakreshvara, Sri Murari and Haridasa!

4Glory to Sarvabhauma, Kashi Mishra and Ramananda!
Glory to Vasudeva Ghosha, Madhava and Mukunda!

5Glory to Dhananjaya and Sri Svarupa Damodara!
Glory to Narahari, Gauridasa and Kashishvara!

6Glory to Gadadhara Dasa, Shridhara and Vijaya!
Glory to Shuklambara Brahmachari and Sri Sanjaya!1

7Glory to Gopala Bhatta, Sri Rupa and Sanatana!
Glory to Raghunatha Dasa, the life of the sorrowful!

8Glory to Sri Bhugarbha, Lokanatha and Sri Raghava!
Glory to Raghunatha Bhatta and Yadava Acharya!

9Glory, glory to Sri Jiva, the treasury of virtues!
Glory to the merciful Krishnadasa Kaviraja!

10Glory, glory to Srinivasa Acharya Thakura!
Glory to Narottama, whose greatness is boundless!

11Glory, glory to Shyamananda, whose deeds are limitless,
whose former name was Sri Duhkhini Krishnadasa!2

12Glory to the Vaishnavas, the utmost limit of mercy,
by whose grace all perfection is attained!3

13Glory, glory to the listeners, the abode of virtues!
Now listen with kind hearts to what I shall tell.

14Srinivasa Acharya, taking the jewel-like books,
goes along the road to Gauda, remembering Gauranga.

15With him is Narottama — such that only their bodies are different;
and Shyamananda — the object of the Acharya's deepest affection.

16Srinivasa, with Narottama and Shyamananda,
goes along the road without obstacle, rejoicing.

17Finding a company of people going to Nilachala,
they travel with them along the forest road.

18Especially: the path by which Sri Chaitanya went —
by that path Sanatana went to Nilachala.4

19Asking in place after place where the Lord and [His] servant had stayed,
they look at all those places, losing their composure.

20Travelling the forest road is the greatest joy;
on no day and nowhere does any danger arise.

21In which lands and in which villages they stayed —
for fear of the book growing too long, I have not written it.

22Everywhere the word spread: "A certain merchant
is going to Nilachala, carrying great wealth with him."

23The robbers of King Vira Hambira5 carefully
made their calculations and saw: the cart was full of all kinds of jewels.6

24They went and tell the king: "A certain merchant
is carrying a cartful of priceless jewels."

25Hearing it from the robbers' mouths, the king was delighted.
What the king's conduct was like, I shall tell a little.

26He is always robbing, taking robbers with him;
seeing him, people tremble with fear all the time.

27And of his other misdeeds there is no end in the telling;
there is only one [good thing]: he listens to the Puranas from a brahmana.

28So Vira Hambira commanded his formidable robbers:
"Get ready and go right now.

29Bring the cart with the wealth here secretly;
frighten them, but take no one's life."

30Receiving the king's order, the robbers set off;
seeing them, decent folk tremble.

31As the king is, so are all these followers of his:
robbing is their constant delight.

32Going from Vana-Vishnupura to distant lands,
they joined all these travellers unnoticed.

33Srinivasa Acharya and the others, together with the cart,
pass through Panchakuta7 and go along the road to Vishnupura.

34"We have reached our own country without obstacle" — so they reason;
that the king in Vishnupura is wicked, this they do not know.

35Near the capital, Vana-Vishnupura,
in the middle of the forest is a large village — there they came.

36Eating and their other tasks they finished while it was still day,
and half the night they spent in the joy of talk about Krishna.

37That night all lay down to sleep
and fell asleep — quite unaware.

38The decent villagers think to themselves:
"Will Krishna protect this merchant?

39They are all at ease, they know no danger;
and we cannot even warn them — we fear the king.

40Here the wicked king, for the sake of a little wealth,
sends his robbers very far afield.

41How did this merchant, with a cartful of wealth,
come along the road and get through?"

42Someone says: "This is a righteous merchant;
that is why the robbers cannot steal his wealth."

43Someone says: "The robbers are following on his heels;
who knows when they will come and attack."

44So people say many things, staying in their homes.
Here, meanwhile, the robbers ponder various schemes.

45Someone says: "Hey, brothers, do this deed,
so that we are not shamed among the brotherhood of robbers.

46Near the village of Tamar8 you made ready,
but there you could not carry out your task.

47Near Raghunathpur,9 in the night,
you were all defeated before them.

48Now you have come near Vana-Vishnupura:
whatever strength and wits each of you has — show it here.

49If today we give that king the cart with the wealth,
he will be pleased; otherwise he will kill us all."

50Saying this, all gathering together
worship Chandi,10 offering her goats, sheep, buffaloes and other victims.

51Bowing at Chandi's feet they say again and again:
"Grant us success and protect us all."

52Saying much in this way, they sent ahead, to where the Acharya and the others were,
one of their best thieves.

53He came and sees: all have fallen asleep;
knowing the moment was right, he went and informed the robbers.

54The robbers came quickly in fearsome guise,
and, freely taking the cart, entered the forest.

55At the end of the night, entering Vana-Vishnupura,
they told the king the whole story.

56All the decent folk of Vana-Vishnupura
heard that the king had stolen great wealth.

57Sitting in seclusion, someone says to another:
"The evil-minded king has done a very wicked deed.

58From Vrindavana a merchant with his wealth
was going to the Kshetra for the darshan of Jagannatha.

59This sinful villain has brought him grief;
I understand: there will never be deliverance for him."

60Someone says into another's ear, weeping:
"Vana-Vishnupura will go to ruin.

61There is no king so wicked in the land of Bharata;
no one is able to punish this sinner."

62Someone says: "This is the way of this wicked king:
he will suffer in hell, there will never be any way out for him."

63Someone says: "All this wicked man does is wrong;
tell me, how can any good come to him?"

64Someone says: "The giver of good is Lord Narayana;
the mercy He showed in Kali cannot be described.

65In Navadvipa, in a brahmana family, Jagai and Madhai,
two brothers, the crown jewels of great sinners —11

66those two wretches, for fear of whom people trembled,
the One who sports in Nadia mercifully delivered.

67At their deliverance the gods, mingling with men,
offered so many prayers that there is no end to them.

68Jagai and Madhai became kings among devotees;
who knows how to tell of His extraordinary deeds?"

69Someone says: "That Krishna Chaitanya, Bhagavan,
gave the living beings a jewel rare even for Brahma and the others.

70That Lord has hidden Himself in Nilachala;
who now will deliver such a wicked man?"

71Someone says: "Hey, brother, I tell you:
such a wicked man is saved by the mercy of His devotee."

72Someone says: "The sight of such a devotee is rare;
why would he come to this sinful land?"

73Someone says: "The scriptures say this is the devotee's way:
to deliver the living beings he wanders through every land.

74Through the devotee that Lord accomplishes all things;
without the devotee's mercy there is never success."

75Someone says: "Ah, this is what I feel:
surely some great soul will come here.

76By a particle of his mercy not a trace of sorrow will remain;
evil thinking will vanish, and the king will become a Vaishnava."

77Saying this, they pray to the Lord again and again:
"Put an end to the king's lawless conduct."

78So the decent folk think of [the king's] welfare.
Here, meanwhile, the king rejoices at home at gaining the wealth.

79Greatly pleased with the robbers,
he gave them clothes and ornaments, praising them.

80King Sri Vira Hambira reflects in his mind:
"This cart is surely from the western land.

81For many days I have gained much wealth,
but such joy has never arisen in my heart.

82I understand: there are priceless jewels in it."
Saying this, he looks toward the chest of books.

83Quickly opening the chest of books himself,
he sees the jewel-books inside the chest.

84As soon as he saw the books, his mind became pure;
again and again he gazes at the jewel-books.

85Astonished, the king says to the astrologer:12
"How did you make your reckoning? Tell me."

86He says, "Maharaja, whenever I reckon,
at once I see that there are priceless jewels in this."

87Hearing this, the king says, "Do not fear at all:
whatever you reckon at any time all proves true.

88What you reckoned now as well is no false word:
in every way these are priceless jewels.

89These priceless jewels are obtained only by great fortune."
Saying much like this, he looks at the robbers.

90Anxious, he says to the robbers again and again,
"Did you kill anyone? Tell me the truth."

91The robbers say, "They were all asleep;
we brought the cart away — none of them knew.

92You yourself forbade us earlier:
why should we take lives? So the task was done in this way."

93Hearing this, the king grew steady and says to the brahmanas:
"The evil deed I have done has borne its fruit at last.

94I have caused pain in the heart of some great soul;
in the fire of his anger I shall surely be burnt to ashes.

95If I obtain the darshan of the acharya of these books,
then I shall take shelter at his feet.

96O brothers, this is what comes to my sinful mind:
he will surely show me mercy."

97Saying this, he sent messengers to search,
and carefully kept the jewel-books together with the cart.

98Hearing about the books, the king's wife
herself became eager to see them.

99What shall I say? With the arrival of the jewel-books
the king's palace shone exceedingly.

100Suddenly auspiciousness spread through Vishnupura;
all the evil endeavours of the people vanished.

101King Vira Hambira always had this in mind:
"When shall I see him whose books these are?"

102Thinking thus, the king became agitated;
at that very moment the goddess of sleep drew him away.

103As if in a dream he sees a beautiful person
whose wondrous body surpasses a mountain of gold.13

104With his moon-like face he says, smiling and smiling,
"Do not worry: he will come and meet you.

105His heart will be pleased with you;
birth after birth be his servant."

106Saying this, he vanished, and at that moment
the king's sleep broke; the king floats in tears.

107"What did I see, what did I see!" he says again and again;
he looks in all four directions, but does not reveal the secret.

108Meanwhile, when the robbers had taken away the cart of books,
suddenly sleep broke, and everyone awoke.

109Srinivasa Acharya and the others at dawn
search here and there in distress.

110Finding no trace, they weep;
"What thunderbolt has struck!" says everyone.

111Narottama says, "I shall give up my life."
Shyamananda says, "I shall enter this fire."

112What came into the mind of Srinivasa Acharya —
the heart breaks to tell of it; what shall I say of it?

113All the people who were with them, with aching hearts,
resolved: "We will not go home any more."

114The news of the theft of the books became known everywhere;
the Acharya and the others sank in an ocean of great sorrow.

115After some time, all of them, taking courage,
said to one another what cannot be described.

116Suddenly someone says to Srinivasa,
"You will find the books in Vishnupura; go to the king."

117Hearing these words, joy arose in his mind;
and besides, he sees various auspicious signs.

118Understanding the Lord's design, consoling everyone,
Srinivasa says to Sri Narottama:

119"Go quickly to the village of Kheturi
and carry out the order of Prabhu Lokanatha.

120Send Shyamananda in good company:
by way of Ambika he will go to Utkala.

121When the books are recovered, I will send word;
do not be anxious: you will come, and we shall all meet."

122Saying much like this, he sent the two away;
how distressed the two were cannot be described.

123Not transgressing the Acharya's word, the two
went to the village of Kheturi; their minds are not at peace.

124Who can understand this lila of the Mahashaya? On arriving, the very first thing he did was to infuse spiritual power (shakti) into Sri Santosha.14

125At the sight of Sri Narottama all the people
became greatly joyful and forgot their grief and sorrow.

126With great care keeping the two in complete seclusion,
the wise, hearing the story of the theft of the books, were grieved.

127Here Srinivasa, having sent the two away,
became distressed, unable to hold his heart.

128Leaving his companions elsewhere,
he quickly entered Vana-Vishnupura alone.

129Who will understand the heart of the mahanta?
In search of the books he wanders alone.

130Here and there people say to one another,
"A wondrous person has come to Vishnupura.

131Is he a god, or a portion of the Lord?
Seeing his beauty, whose composure is not shattered?"

132Saying this, to have the darshan of the Acharya
people run from all four directions in delight.

133A brahmana's son named Sri Krishnavallabha —
at the darshan of the Acharya prema arose in him.15

134He took him to his own house in Deuli
and surrendered himself at the Acharya's lotus feet.

135Whatever Acharya Thakura asked him,
he told it all in order and in detail.

136"The king is listening to the Bhagavata" — hearing this,
he goes to the royal assembly, taking Krishnavallabha with him.

137Seeing the Acharya's radiance, the king respectfully
fell to the ground, bowed, and considered himself blessed.

138He had a wonderful seat brought and seated him;
the Acharya forbids him to ask anything:

139"O king, when the discourse on the Bhagavata is finished,
whatever you ask, I will tell you."

140Saying, "As you command," the king reflects in his mind:
"He is surely the keeper of these jewel-books.16

141By my good fortune he has suddenly appeared before me;
I shall surrender myself at his feet."

142Thinking thus, the king gazes with fixed eyes;
at the end the Acharya said something to the king.

143The king's mind had already become pure;
he asks to hear the true meaning:

144"O mahashaya, this is what is in my mind:
explain a verse of the Bhagavata with your own blessed mouth."

145Hearing the king's words, Acharya Thakura
knew that the king's evil mind had gone far away.

146The Acharya says, "What does your mind wish to hear?"
The king says, "Please speak something of the Bhramara-gita."17

147At the king's words he was immersed in happiness;
the king's reader placed the book before him.

148Acharya Thakura carefully began the reading;
he poured a nectar-rain of unheard-of, wondrous meanings.

149In the assembly tears flow from everyone's eyes;
King Sri Vira Hambira was overwhelmed.

150The king's reader, named Vyasa Chakravarti —
who can tell what longing seized him?

151All who were there at the time of the holy discourse —
from their manifestations prema arose in others as well.

152Acharya Thakura forgot himself;
he cannot become steady, so great is his absorption.

153Sri Vira Hambira, falling at the Acharya's feet,
is not steady, even though the discourse has concluded.

154After some time, becoming composed, he thinks in his mind:
"I have committed a terrible offence at these feet."

155Thus immersed in the rasa of humility, Sri Vira Hambira
floats in tears and cannot become steady.

156Giving the Acharya lodging in a very secluded place,
at evening he quickly went and met him.

157Bowing with joined palms, he makes his request:
"Prabhu, tell me in detail how you came."

158Hearing these words, the Acharya with a joyful heart
says to the king, "Now I shall tell you briefly.

159Svayam Bhagavan Krishna, the prince of Vraja,
concealed His manifest pastimes in Vraja.

160When the time came, taking with Him His angas and upangas,18
He descended in Navadvipa in great joy.

161In Navadvipa the Lord performed wondrous pastimes;
Shesha, Shiva and others cannot describe them.

162What is attested in the scriptures He made directly visible;
with the sacrifice of sankirtana He made the world mad with joy.

163After living for some time at home with His associates,
He took sannyasa from Keshava Bharati.19

164He became renowned by the name Sri Krishna Chaitanya;
to show mercy to living beings He travelled to all the holy places.

165To give happiness to His devotees He resided in Nilachala;
there is the wondrous play of the moving and the unmoving Brahman.20

166His dear devotees, viziers of the king of Gauda,21
possessed of great wealth, great and profound panditas —

167Rupa and Sanatana, whose names are known throughout the world —
renouncing everything, went to Vrindavana.

168They lived there at Mahaprabhu's command
and, following the scriptures, recovered the lost holy places of Vraja.

169They composed many books, an ocean of nectar;
they opened the treasury of the jewels of the pastimes of Vraja.

170How many meanings of the Srimad-Bhagavatam and other [works] they revealed —
how much of it could I tell with a single mouth?

171I, utterly unworthy, born in Gauda,
went to Vrindavana at the command of the Lords.

172I became a disciple of Sri Gopala Bhatta Gosvami
and studied the books of the Gosvamis.

173Sri Jiva Gosvami and other greatly wise ones
entrusted [the books to me] to make them known in Gauda.

174I carefully brought them to this land;
some distance [from here], at the end of the night, the books were stolen.

175All together we searched for them everywhere;
in many ways we held on to patience.

176There is a king's son named Narottama —
of supreme renunciation, versed in all the scriptures.

177And one named Shyamananda, mature in every respect;
those two I sent each to his own land.

178The armed Vrajavasis who are with me
I have left all in one place, giving them lodging.

179For the sake of the books I wandered everywhere;
hearing of the Purana recitation, I came here.

180I have told something of what happened — what more is there to say?
Without the books my heart is breaking."

181Hearing these words of Srinivasa Acharya,
the king, distraught, falls at his holy feet.

182Weeping, he says: "I am the chief of robbers;
the evil deeds I have done I cannot tell.

183When you, Prabhu, came by the forest road,
I received the news then and there from the mouths of messengers.

184For the sake of [the expected] gain I rejoiced;
I had an astrologer calculate — he determined with certainty:

185'A very great mahajana is bringing great jewels;22
with little searching they will surely be obtained.'

186Hearing these words, I sent the robbers;
'Take no one's life' — this much I said.

187The robbers brought the cart without trouble;
seeing the chest, I was overjoyed.

188Opening the chest, I see the jewels of books;
at the mere sight of them my mind was turned.

189I grew eager to see the keeper of the books
and quickly sent messengers to search for him.

190You, Prabhu, know the hearts, you are the purifier of the fallen;
to me, a lowly one, you suddenly granted your darshan.

191At the mere sight of you I surrendered myself at your feet;
forgive my offence and be merciful to me.

192Seeing what a great sinner I am, do not scorn me;
do what will free me from sin."

193Saying this, he fell at the Acharya's feet
and bathes the Acharya's feet with his tears.

194Seeing how deeply distressed the king's heart was,
the Acharya showed him the utmost favour.

195In endless conversation the night turned to dawn;
what can be said — the ocean of prema surged.

196The king quickly brought those people of the Acharya
and gave them lodging in a lovely place.

197The king carefully had the Acharya bathed
and took him to where the jewels of books were.

198The Acharya's mind blossomed with great joy;
the bliss [he felt] on seeing the books cannot be described.

199The king, having the books worshipped in various ways,
took the Acharya into the inner apartments.

200The king's wife, seeing the Acharya —
how overwhelmed with joy she was, I do not know how to tell.

201Bowing at the Acharya's two feet,
she considers herself blessed and floats in tears.

202Sri Acharya, having shown mercy to the king's wife,
came with the king to the secluded lodging.

203Again and again the king says, falling at his feet:
"Because of the evil deed I did, my heart knows no peace."

204Knowing the king's heart, Acharya Thakura
says again and again: "Put away all worry.

205I have entrusted you to the feet of Sri Krishna Chaitanya;
meditate on those lotus feet within your heart.

206Always considering yourself an offender,
perform this nama-sankirtana without cease."

207Saying this, to remove all the king's distress,
he instructed him in the Harinama maha-mantra.23

208Again he says to the king with sweet words:
"Always be attentive in hearing and chanting.

209Sri Krishna Chaitanya Prabhu, the purifier of the world,
distributed this mantra of the Name to living beings.

210O king, after the relishing of the Gosani's books24
I will give you initiation into the mantra of Radha and Krishna."

211Saying this and telling him a little about the angas of bhakti,
he set at rest the heart of King Vira Hambira.

212The king together with his family, with joy in his heart,
sold himself at the feet of Srinivasa Acharya.

213The stolen books found, the robber king delivered —
this news spread everywhere.

214Sri Krishnavallabha, Vyasa and all the others
took shelter at the Acharya's lotus feet.

215An ocean of joy surged in Vishnupura;
Bhakti-devi showed her favour in every house.

216By the qualities of Sri Krishna Chaitanya, Nityananda and Advaita
all are overwhelmed and know nothing else.25

217Gadadhara, Srivasa and all the other Prabhus —
with the names and qualities of them all they are ceaselessly intoxicated.

218A wondrous longing to see Vaishnavas grew;26
deep attachment arose for Navadvipa and Vrindavana.

219Singing the glory of Srinivasa Acharya,
they are immersed in such joy — who can describe it?

220Everyone praises his own good fortune,
and all ceaselessly perform kirtana of the holy Name.

221King Sri Vira Hambira, with joy in his heart,
joining his palms, says to the Acharya:

222"O Prabhu, you have removed our sorrow;
you have bestowed a jewel hard for the gods to attain.

223O Prabhu, now I submit at your holy feet:
that the books were stolen, everyone came to know.

224That the books are found and I, a lowly robber, am subdued —
kindly write a letter about this and send it to Vrindavana.

225And let the Gosvamis know this too:
that they all may show mercy to me, a sinner.

226Where Sri Thakura Narottama and Shyamananda are —
let there be [your] order to send such a letter there too."

227Hearing the king's words, the Acharya, who had already
written a letter himself, gave it into the king's hands.

228Seeing the letter, the king was exceedingly glad;
Acharya Thakura again says to the king:

229"The people who came with the cart from Vraja —
they will leave quickly, taking the cart."

230Saying this, the Acharya himself, with care,
gave the letter to his companions, instructing them at length.

231The king bowed to the ground before all those people;
the honour he showed them — who can describe it?

232On the very cart on which the great jewels of books had come,
he carefully placed various goods.

233For Sri Govinda, Gopinatha and Madanamohana
and for all the other places he gave them, dividing them up.

234Taking those goods, the armed men
took their leave and quickly set off.

235All of them with the cart, in great delight,
reaching Vrindavana, gave the letter to the Gosvami.

236They told all the news from beginning to end;
hearing it, everyone's anxiety was dispelled.

237Learning the detailed news by reading the letter,
in great joy, saying much, they wish [them] well.

238The goods that Sri Vira Hambira had sent
Sri Jiva Gosvami distributed everywhere.

239With the thought "Srinivasa will send a letter,"27
Sri Jiva Gosvami is in great joy at every moment.

240Meanwhile King Sri Vira Hambira, making haste,
sent his master's letter to Kheturi.

241Sri Thakura Mahashaya, together with Shyamananda,
distressed with worry, is staying in seclusion.28

242Coming to the village of Kheturi, the messenger asks,
"Where is Sri Thakura Mahashaya?

243Sri Acharya Prabhu has sent a letter
from Vana-Vishnupura — let him know of this quickly."

244Hearing this, someone quickly informed Mahashaya:
"A man has come from Vana-Vishnupura;

245he has with him a letter from Acharya Prabhu."
On hearing these words — what joy! There is no end to it.

246Calling the messenger near, [Mahashaya] asks after their welfare.
The messenger says, "All is supremely well, Mahashaya."

247Hearing this, Shyamananda floats in tears of joy;
stretching out both arms, he embraces the messenger.

248The messenger, in great haste, having given the letter to Mahashaya,
fell at the feet of both, rolling on the ground.

249Reading the letter and learning all the news,
[Mahashaya] cannot contain in his heart his boundless joy.

250To King Santosha Datta, the son of his paternal uncle,
he told it briefly in sweet words, like this:

251"The books were soon recovered in Vana-Vishnupura;
Sri Acharya has shown mercy to Sri Vira Hambira."

252Hearing of the recovery of the books and the deliverance of King Vira Hambira,
Santosha was comforted in mind and heart.

253In supreme bliss Sri Santosha, the best of the wise,
showed great honor to the king's messenger.

254He heard everything from him, from beginning to end,
and spent much wealth on the performance of auspicious rites.

255Seeing Santosha's conduct, everyone was amazed;
Sri Thakura Mahashaya was delighted.

256Seating Sri Shyamananda beside him,
he wrote a letter to Sri Acharya Srinivasa.

257In it he revealed the state of his heart
and made known that Shyamananda would go to Utkala.

258To Sri Vira Hambira he wrote a separate letter;
in it he proclaimed his supreme good fortune.

259Taking the two letters, the messenger went to Vishnupura;
giving the letters to the king, he reported everything.

260The king, praising his messenger's good fortune,
goes before Sri Acharya, full of delight.

261Meanwhile Srinivasa Acharya, gathering his disciples,
is having them study the books of the Gosvamis.

262He sits in the midst of the assembly like the sun;
whose eyes are not gladdened at the sight of that beauty?

263Sri Vira Hambira, coming before Sri Acharya,
bowed with care, prostrating on the ground.

264Standing with joined palms, he says to the Acharya,
"A letter came from Kheturi this morning.

265Showing great mercy to me, a sinner,
Thakura Mahashaya has written this letter.

266He wrote this letter to Prabhu" — saying this,
he handed over the letter, full of great delight.

267The Acharya reads the letter, and all the people listen;
no one can hold back the tears in their eyes.

268When the letter had been read, the king further reported
what, beyond the letter, he had heard from the messenger's mouth:

269how Raja Sri Santosha himself, with enthusiasm,
performed auspicious rites in various ways,

270and in what manner he gave gifts to the brahmanas —
hearing all this, everyone felt great joy.

271A letter from Mahashaya had come to the king —
at this, everyone praises the monarch's good fortune.

272After staying some time in the Acharya's assembly,
the king, taking leave, quickly went home.

273Reading Sri Mahashaya's letter in private,
the king, overwhelmed, cannot be calm.

274At that time the queen came and makes a request:
"Be kind and let me hear the letter."

275Hearing the queen's words, the king at that very moment
read the letter to her with a most delighted heart.

276As soon as she heard it, the queen forgets herself;
she prays to Providence again and again:

277"O lord! Thakura Mahashaya Narottama —
mercifully show him even once to me, a lowly one!"29

278Saying this, the queen, bathed in tears,
fell at the king's feet, rolling on the ground.

279She says to the king, "Now your life has found its purpose:
without effort you have gained the treasure of prema for Krishna's feet."

280The king says, "That treasure is exceedingly rare.
Will it touch me? I am a great abode of sin.

281I, a wicked man, have spent this birth in vain;
there is no counting the offenses I have committed."

282Saying this, the king, his heart losing all composure,
crying "Sri Krishna Chaitanya!", rolls on the ground.

283Crying "Prabhu Nityananda, Sri Advaita Prabhu!",
he laments bitterly again, raising both arms.

284"Gadadhara, Srivasa, Svarupa, Vakreshvara,
Haridasa, Murari, Mukunda, Damodara,30

285Gauridasa, Kashishvara, Rupa-Sanatana" —
taking all these names, he weeps.

286Heaving a long sigh, he again says to the queen,
"There is no one in the world so foolish as I.

287In Navadvipa the Lord, the eternal complete Brahman,
performed wondrous pastimes with His dear ones.

288Hearing of that Lord's pastimes, my heart did not melt;
how many false arguments I made — such were my deeds.

289I do not know in what auspicious moment I stole the books —
because of that I obtained Srinivasa Acharya Prabhu.

290He melted a lump of iron such as I;
in his mercy he plunged me into that ocean of pastimes.

291My lord Srinivasa is the very limit of compassion;
he will fulfill whatever desire may arise [in the heart].

292Do not worry: you will meet his dear ones.
Make those feet the essence [of all] in life and in death."

293Thus the king says much and praises the queen;
I cannot tell it at length for fear of making the book too long.

294Meanwhile Mahashaya, having joyfully sent off the letter,
is eager to see the Acharya.

295In the absorption of affection he reflects within himself:
"How shall I remain calm without Shyamananda?

296Tomorrow morning Shyamananda will leave for Utkala."
Reflecting thus, he became wet with tears.

297Sri Thakura Narottama is the embodiment of affection;
what his affection for Shyamananda is like — where is my power to tell it?

298After a while, becoming calm, he says to Shyamananda,
"At daybreak you will certainly set out.

299When you reach your country, quickly send a letter here;
I shall meet you there, going to Nilachala."

300Shyamananda had been extremely distressed;
hearing these words, he rejoiced in his mind.

301Sri Thakura Narottama, together with Shyamananda,
spent the day and night absorbed in prema.

302Taking courage, at daybreak
he sends Shyamananda off to Utkala.

303He gave him a man as companion, with money and other things;
at the moment of departure he became greatly distressed.

304Shyamananda, wet with the tears of his eyes,
bows to Narottama, falling to the ground.

305Likewise Sri Thakura Narottama, bowing,
floats in tears as he embraces Shyamananda.

306What Mahashaya became after sending off Shyamananda —
that cannot be put into words.

307The people of the village of Kheturi run in all directions;
all are distressed at Shyamananda's departure.

308Sri Raja Santosha Datta, together with his people,
bowing to Shyamananda, showed great humility.

309Shyamananda embraced Santosha;
at the farewell, tears could not be held back.

310Sri Raja Santosha, going to the bank of the Padmavati,
floats in tears as he seats him in the boat.31

311The most steadfast Shyamananda, boarding the boat,
crossed the Padmavati, his heart losing all composure.

312There, after bathing and so on and staying a while,
he bowed to the Padmavati and set off.

313Having darshan of Gauranga at Kantaka-nagara,
he went by way of Navadvipa to Shantipura.32

314In what places which devotees showed him favor —
for fear of the book's length I have not described.

315Quickly going to Ambika-nagara,
he went to the abode of his master, absorbed in prema.

316What joy there was at the sight of Sri Hridaya Chaitanya's feet —
who can describe it?

317He, showing great favor to Shyamananda,
showed him Sri Krishna Chaitanya and Nityananda.33

318Shyamananda, having darshan of the two Lords,
was overwhelmed — his tears could not be held back.

319The two Lords abide in silent form;
They showed Shyamananda great favor.

320What do I know, to tell of the pastimes of these Lords,
to whose service Sri Pandita Gauridasa is devoted?

321In this connection I shall tell a little of the Pandita's ways —
he to whose prema the Lord is subject, as is known in the world.

322Gauridasa Pandita is supremely full of prema;
he is Sri Subalachandra, the abode of virtues.34

323Sri Subala, dear to Krishna, is supremely beautiful;
his character and the rest the best of the wise describe with care.

324Thus [it is said] in the Sri [Bhakti-]rasamrita-sindhu, in the Pashchima-vibhaga, in the third lahari, the seventeenth verse: "Him who has conquered gold by the lustre of his body, dear to Hari, wearing a necklace, clad in green — Subala, whose eyes are like blue lotuses, who delights his friends by the wisdom of his conduct, I praise."

325Thus [it is said] in the Stavavali, in the Vraja-vilasa, the twenty-second verse:
"He who, from the fullness of deep attachment, out of fear of separation,
does not let go of the hand of the Moon of Gokula even in dreams,
whose heart is sprinkled by the waterfall of Radhika's love —
to that Subala, whose body is overwhelmed by prema, I bow."

326Thus [it is said] in the Sri Ujjvala-nilamani, in the [section] on the kinds of helpers, the seventh verse:35 "Having appeased her, he brings back the lovely girl who had gone off after a playful quarrel; in the grove-bower he makes for the Destroyer of Agha a bed fit for the pastimes of Kandarpa; Him, bathed in perspiration, His limbs exhausted, upon His beloved's breast, he fans — in what service does glorious Subala not find himself qualified?"

327That Sri Subala is Gauridasa is known everywhere.
Non-different [from Subala], he is the beloved of Chaitanya and Nityananda.

328Thus [it is said] in the Sri Gaura-ganoddesha-dipika (128):
"Subala, the best of the dear [friends], is Gauridasa Pandita."

329And elsewhere:36
"Him who was formerly Subalachandra, Sri Gauridasa, endowed with virtues,
the beloved of Sri Krishna Chaitanya and Nityananda, I worship."

330Suryadasa Sarakhel is a magnanimous pandita;
his brother is the renowned Gauridasa Pandita.37

331Having told his elder brother, he came from Shaligrama
to Ambika and settled on the bank of the Ganga.

332Supremely detached, he always stays in solitude;
the Lord knows well the Pandita's state of mind.

333One day Gaura-raya, from Shantipura,
crossing the Ganga, came to Ambika.

334He says to the Pandita: "I had gone to Shantipura;
coming to the village of Harinadi, I boarded a boat.38

335I crossed the Ganga, rowing the boat with the oar.
Here, take the oar: now I have given it to you.

336Ferry the living beings across the river of worldly existence."
Saying this, He embraced the Pandita.

337Taking the Pandita with Him, the Lord went to Nadia
and immersed [him] in most wondrous pastimes.

338Who can understand the ways of Gaurachandra?
He gave the Pandita His own nectarean Gita.39

339After some days the Pandita, coming to Ambika,
constantly reads the Gita given by the Lord.

340The Gita in the letters of the Lord's own sacred hand —
the happiness of seeing it I cannot express.

341The Gita given by the Lord and the oar, in the presence of the Lords,
the fortunate see in Ambika even today.

342There is no end to telling the Pandita's fair fame;
his all in all is Krishna Chaitanya and Nitai.

343He is always intoxicated with singing the qualities of Nitai and Chaitanya;
apart from Nitai and Chaitanya he knows no other.

344Nitai and Chaitanya are the two pupils of his eyes;
what can others know of this wondrous stream of prema?

345I do not know what bliss grows when he beholds Them;
without Them for even a moment, sorrow knows no bounds.

346Knowing the Pandita's heart, the Lord Gaurahari
one day says to the Pandita earnestly:

347"Have a neem tree brought from Navadvipa
and make Me together with My brother.40

348Without difficulty the two Deities will be made;
I will surely fulfil your desire."

349Hearing this, the Pandita was overjoyed
and with care had the wooden Deities made.

350The one who made Them is a recipient of the Lord's mercy;
[the Lord] manifests Himself — the other's [part] is a mere pretext.

351Seeing the wondrous Deities, the magnanimous Pandita
lost all composure; streams flow from his eyes unceasingly.

352Considering himself blessed, together with his dear ones
he prepares the rite of abhisheka.

353According to custom and scripture, at an auspicious moment,
having performed the abhisheka of the Deities, he seated [Them] on the throne.

354Beholding Nitai and Chaitanyachand,
the Lord's dear ones were immersed in great bliss.

355The forms of the two Lords enchant the worlds;
apart from the circle of devotees, this is beyond the reach of others.

356Nitai and Chaitanya are subject to Gauridasa's prema —
this story spread through the world day and night.

357The lila that Nitai and Chaitanya manifest in Gauridasa's house
is known throughout the world.

358What do I know, to tell of the Pandita's intent?
He is ceaselessly immersed in the service of the two Lords.

359One day Nitai and Chaitanya, absorbed in prema,
smiling gently, say to Gauridasa:

360"Who will understand your ways?
Overwhelmed by prema, you do not know yourself.

361O friend Subala! Do you not remember all that —
the fun of grazing the cows on the sandbanks of the Yamuna?"

362Saying many such things, the two Lords, abodes of prema,
took dark and white forms — those of Krishna and Balarama.

363Horn, staff, flute, ornaments of peacock feathers —
what beauty of the cowherd dress, enchanting the worlds!

364Seeing this, Gauridasa forgot himself;
he is intoxicated with that mood — who will understand such ways?

365By the Lord's will, becoming steady after a while,
he sees Nitai and Chaitanyachand on the throne.

366Thus the two Lords perform various sports;
Gauridasa in his delight cannot keep his body still.

367One day Gauridasa, having cooked,
says to the two Lords: "Please eat."

368Hearing such gentle words from the Pandita,
They do not eat, but remain silent.

369Seeing the Lords' manner, Pandita Thakura,
somewhat in anger, speaks sweet words:

370"If You find happiness in Your hearts without eating,
then why do You make me cook?"

371Saying this, Gauridasa remains silent;
smiling, the Lords say to the Pandita softly, softly:

372"Your cooking is never settled with a little:
you make rice and the rest and many kinds of vegetable dishes.

373You do not heed Our forbidding, and We cannot bear to see your toil.
Whatever comes without effort — that is best of all."

374Gauridasa says: "I shall never do so;
I shall boil just one dish of greens (shak) and feed You."

375Hearing the Pandita's words, the two Lords laugh;
They eat and, delighted, say a little:

376"How did you cook these wondrous greens?
We are satisfied by eating just one dish of greens."

377Praising thus, both of Them eat;
the Pandita, seeing that sport, refreshes his eyes.

378One day Gauridasa, with joy in his heart,
longed to put some ornaments on [Them].

379Knowing the Pandita's mind, the Lords, delighted,
became adorned with various jewelled ornaments.

380Both stand on the jewelled throne;
the Pandita, entering the temple, saw the splendour —

381he lost all composure, with not a trace of outer awareness;
after a while, becoming steady, he sees the former attire.

382Gauridasa reflects within himself:
"Never have I seen such wondrous ornaments.

383I had the desire to put ornaments on [Them] —
what could I put on? Now that delusion is dispelled."

384As he reflected thus, the Lords say to the Pandita:
"With ornaments of flowers the happiness grows exceedingly."

385Hearing the very sweet words, the Pandita himself
with great care put the flower ornaments on [Them].

386Garlands hang down, one below another, to the very feet;
it is most charming — there is no end to that beauty.

387The Pandita brought a mirror and set it before the Lords;
how much the delight increased I cannot tell.

388Such deeds of the Pandita spread through the world;
I have told a little of this to purify myself.

389The disciple of such a Pandita is Hridaya Chaitanya,
who knows no one but Pandita Thakura.

390Formerly all knew him by the name of Sri Hridayananda;
ceaselessly he serves the Lord with care.

391How the name Hridaya Chaitanya came about,
and what the Pandita's mercy was, I tell briefly.

392One day, as the night gave way to dawn, Gauridasa
came to Gadadhara Pandita.

393Gadadhara Pandita, seeing Gauridasa,
with no end of affection seated him by his side.

394Smiling gently, he says again and again:
"Today at dawn I have seen my good fortune."

395Gauridasa replies in very sweet words:
"Good fortune will be mine — that is why I have come."

396Pandita Gadai says: "With what shall I please you?"
Gauridasa says: "I shall ask for it and take it."

397Gadadhara says: "All this is yours;
whatever you wish, take it — what is there to consider?"

398Pandita Thakura says: "I want Hridaya."
Hearing this, Pandita Gosani calls Hridaya.41

399Hridayananda came with a joyful heart
and, falling to the ground, bowed at the feet of both.

400Pandita Gosani, having said many things to Hridaya,
entrusted [him] to Gauridasa Pandita.42

401How great Pandita Gosani's mercy to Sri Hridaya was
is known everywhere; who can tell how great [it was]?

402He had raised him from childhood
and in a short time had him study the scriptures.

403He was overwhelmed with parental love, yet did not act from the feeling "he is mine":
having given [him] to Pandita Thakura, he rejoiced.43

404The way of Pandita Gadai and Gauridasa —
who has the power to know it without the Lord's mercy?

405For some time Gauridasa remained beside Gadadhara,
[absorbed] in the rasa of talks about the Lord's pastimes.

406Taking leave of Pandita Gosani,
he came back to his residence, taking Hridayananda with him.

407After some days he gave Hridaya the mantra of initiation
and entrusted him to the feet of Nityananda and Chaitanya.

408Hridaya became absorbed in the service of the Lord;
seeing this, Gauridasa rejoices at heart.

409Who will understand the play of Gauridasa Pandita?
Moment after moment so many waves of prema rise [in him]!

410One day he says to Hridayananda:
"The time of the Lord's birth festival has come.44

411I will arrange all that is needed at a disciple's house
and come back to the residence soon — such is my intention.

412Always be attentive in the service of the Lord."
Saying this, he set out from the residence.

413Intoxicated with the rasa of the Lord's wondrous pastimes,
he wanders in seclusion with his dear companions.

414At the residence Hridayananda thinks to himself:
"Why has Prabhu delayed so many days?45

415Here many provisions have already been made ready,
and only about two days remain before the festival."

416Thinking thus and remembering Prabhu's feet,
he sent invitations to the festival everywhere.

417On the day before the festival the Pandita came;
hearing about the invitations, he was glad at heart.

418[But,] outwardly angry, he rebukes Hridaya:
"While I am here you have acted on your own —

419you have sent letters of invitation here and there.
What you have done is done, but now you shall not stay here."

420Hearing this, he bowed at [his] two feet,
went to the bank of the Ganga and stayed under a tree.

421Here Gauridasa began the holy festival;
from everywhere all the mahantas came.

422At that time a certain mahajana with care
sent various provisions, filling a boat.

423[This] was made known to Hridayananda on the bank of the Ganga;
he sent word [of it] to Thakura.

424Hearing this, [Thakura,] outwardly angry, says: "Go and tell [him]:
let him hold the festival, taking all those provisions."

425Receiving the guru's order, Hridaya in joy
holds a great festival such as cannot be told.

426The holy Vaishnavas arrived;
all together they perform a wondrous sankirtana.

427The sound of khol and kartals touched the sky,
as if a great ocean of bliss had surged up.

428All the Vaishnavas dance, forming circles;
tears of prema flow ceaselessly from everyone's eyes.

429Nitai and Chaitanya, the two Prabhus full of prema,
dance in the midst of the sankirtana; Hridaya sees [Them].

430What movements in Their dance — they madden the world!
The beauty of the Two lights up the universe.

431The moon-faces of the Two destroy the pride of the moon;
from Hridayananda's eyes bliss rains down.

432The tumult of cries of "Jaya!" in the bliss of the sankirtana —
hearing it, Gauridasa here is overwhelmed with joy.

433The Pandita says softly to Gangadasa:
"It is time for the service; go into the holy temple."

434Bara Gangadasa, entering the holy temple,46
saw the throne empty and came back and told [him].

435Hearing this, what a wondrous emotion arose in the Pandita!
He knew: the two Prabhus are subdued by Hridaya's prema.

436Smiling gently, he took a stick in his hand;
outwardly he shows anger, within is bliss.

437He went to the bank of the Ganga, where the sankirtana was,
and sees the two Prabhus dancing there.

438The two Brothers, seeing the Pandita's anger,
went unnoticed and entered the temple.

439Such is the wondrous pastime of Chaitanyachandra:
He enters the lake of Hridaya's heart — Gauridasa sees [this].47

440Seeing Chaitanyachand in Hridaya's heart,
he cannot hold back his tears; [his] eyes do not blink.

441The outward anger that had been [in him] — he forgot it;
the stick fell from his hand — he did not notice it.

442In the rapture of prema he runs with his arms stretched out
and, his heart rejoicing, embraces Hridaya.

443He says to Hridaya: "You are blessed, blessed!
From today your name is Hridaya Chaitanya."

444Saying this, he bathed [him] in tears;
Hridaya fell and rolled at [his] feet.

445Taking Hridaya Chaitanya with him, Thakura Pandita
came to the courtyard of the Lord's temple.

446What can I say — in what bliss, seeing the sweetness of the two,
he made Hridaya the one in charge of the holy service!

447The bliss of all the Vaishnavas was boundless;
what that great festival was like I cannot describe.

448The mercy [shown] to Hridaya spread through the world;
in this way the name "Hridaya Chaitanya" came about.

449Hridaya Chaitanya is the life of Shyamananda;
by a particle of his mercy what one longs for is fulfilled.

450Showing great mercy to dear Shyamananda,
Hridaya, agitated, sends him off to Utkala.

451Shyamananda, bowing at Prabhu's lotus feet,
in taking leave has his heart awash in tears.

452He made known to Nitai and Chaitanya [what was] in his heart
and, bowing down, became grey with the dust of the courtyard.

453Making many entreaties to Prabhu's associates,
he sets out from Ambika — and cannot walk.

454Seeing his distress, those dear ones of Prabhu
speak many consoling words to Shyamananda:

455"Having distributed Prabhu's jewel of bhakti in Utkala,
you will come to Ambika again when the time comes."

456They say many such things; hearing [them], the son of Durika48
goes to Utkala, meditating on the feet of Sri Guru.

457Ceaselessly he sings the virtues of Nitai and Chaitanya;
himself intoxicated, he intoxicates all.

458Seeing Shyamananda, hosts of great unbelievers
consider themselves blessed and beg for shelter.

459In the land of Gauda there is a village named Dandeshvara,
where formerly Krishna Mandala lived.49

460After that he settled in Utkala.
What can I say of the wondrous pastime at Dandeshvara!

461Shyamananda went by that road;
seeing Shyamananda, everyone's eyes are soothed.

462From there he went quickly to the village of Dharenda50
and became anxious to send auspicious letters.

463To Sri Acharya Thakura and Thakura Mahashaya
he wrote all the news in two letters.

464Sri Mahashaya's man, who had been with him —
giving him the letters, he sent him off with great care.

465Having sent the letters, he manifests prema-bhakti
and, compassionate, makes Utkala blessed.

466Here Sri Thakura Mahashaya, receiving the letter,
read it and joyfully let everyone hear it.

467Mahashaya again, by the hand of that same man,
sent the letter to Sri Acharya in Vishnupura.51

468Having sent the letter, Sri Thakura Mahashaya
sets out for the darshan of Sri Navadvipa and other places.

469Receiving Sri Narottama's letter, the Acharya —
in what a wondrous rapture of affection! — lost his composure.

470Learning the news in Mahashaya's letter,
he reads Sri Shyamananda's letter again and again.

471Some extraordinary deeds of Sri Shyamananda
he made known to everyone in great joy.

472King Sri Vira Hambira, with jubilation in his heart,
taking the letter from Prabhu's side, held it on his head.

473Hearing of Sri Shyamananda's virtues and character,
he longs moment after moment to see him.

474Acharya Thakura, seeing the king's eagerness —
little by little abundant joy grows in his heart.

475Sri Acharya says unhurriedly to the king:
"I shall soon go to Shrikhanda and Yajigrama."

476The king says: "You have made Vana-Vishnupura blessed!
Without Prabhu, Vishnupura will become a wilderness."52

477The Acharya says: "Do not worry at all:
you will soon see [me] in Vana-Vishnupura."

478The king says: "Take me, a wretch, with you."
The Acharya says: "That will be after some days."

479The king says: "I cannot keep [you] by insisting,
and what arises in my mind I cannot even carry out."53

480Having said this, the king could not keep his composure;
Sri Acharya consoled him in many ways.

481Taking heart from the Acharya's words,
he quickly went to his own inner apartments.

482He told the queen all this news;
she says, "Vishnupura will be plunged into darkness."

483The king says, "Now I cannot keep him."
The queen says, "That is true; I have weighed it in my heart.

484The Prabhu will go — how shall I keep my composure?"
As soon as she said this, tears fall from her eyes.

485Sri Vira Hambira, outwardly showing composure,
consoled the queen and went before the Prabhu.

486Everything needed for Acharya Prabhu's journey
the king arranged at that very moment.

487Having prepared everything, with many entreaties
he brought Acharya Prabhu into the inner apartments.

488What the king's wife became at the sight of her own Prabhu —
who could describe it?

489Bowing to the ground, she made many entreaties;
at the time of the Prabhu's departure she sank into an ocean of sorrow.

490Sri Acharya Prabhu, won over by that devotion,
consoled her with great kindness and came back to his lodging.

491"The Acharya is leaving for Yajigrama" —
hearing this, the villagers weep.

492One says to another in great sorrow,
"I see no means to keep him from going."

493Saying many such things, people run to see [him];
all offer their lives at the Acharya's feet.

494Beholding the Acharya to their eyes' fill,
they make entreaties beyond description.

495Sri Acharya Prabhu set out from Vana-Vishnupura
with great wealth.

496The king with his people goes along with him some distance;
the Prabhu commands, "Now go to Vishnupura."

497What the king became in separation from the Prabhu —
who is there who could see it and keep his composure?

498The king with his people went to Vana-Vishnupura,
and Acharya Thakura went on to Yajigrama.

499The news that the Acharya was going to Yajigrama
spread everywhere; people speak of it here and there.

500Hearing that the Acharya is coming home,
the people of Yajigrama came back to life.

501They all went to Lakshmipriya Thakurani
and, overjoyed, told her the news.

502The Acharya's mother, hearing of her son's coming,
was overwhelmed with motherly love beyond description.

503Srinivasa Acharya, entering Yajigrama,
went to where his mother was, watching the road.

504He bowed at the feet of his mother Lakshmipriya;
she looks at her son's face with gladdened eyes.

505Moment by moment her body and mind overflow with joy,
as if a pauper had found a pot full of wealth.

506The people of Yajigrama came running;
seeing Srinivasa, their eyes and hearts were soothed.

507Sri Acharya gladdens everyone with gentle words;
there is a great throng of people at the Acharya's residence.

508When people had come and gone in this way, after that
it became quiet — the beautiful hour of evening.

509With his disciples and others, Sri Acharya in his own home
sat down — what wondrous splendour there was at that time!

510Talk of the books of bhakti is ever on the Acharya's lips;
on every side the pious watch [him] with happiness.

511The wise who lived near Yajigrama and elsewhere,
moved by affection, came to the Acharya's house.

512The Acharya heard that the wise were coming;
he went out to meet them, and there was joy at the meeting.

513Acharya Thakura, bringing them all into the house,
seated them on seats with the greatest respect.54

514The wise Vaishnavas were moved by the Acharya's ways;
they ask the Acharya, in order, all that had happened.

515The Acharya tells how he went to Vrindavana,
how in a dream Rupa and Sanatana showed him mercy,

516how he received the favour of Gopala Bhatta,
how he studied the books of the Gosvamis,

517how he wandered through the land of Vrindavana,
how he came to Gauda with the books,

518how the books were stolen in Vana-Vishnupura,
how the books were recovered, how he came home.

519As they heard all these accounts from beginning to end,
various emotions arose in the hearts of the Vaishnavas.

520All the Vaishnavas, growing calm after a while,
gaze fixedly at Srinivasa's face.

521Srinivasa Acharya, in sweet and gentle words,
asks how the masters here are faring.

522Hearing this, they heave deep sighs and say very slowly,
"Thakura Narahari is all but lifeless.55

523Day and night, in a swoon, he rolls on the ground,
constantly speaks incoherently, and floats in tears.

524Sri Raghunandana and all his dear ones
unceasingly sing the glories of Gora.

525Seeing Thakura's state, who could keep his composure?
What to speak of others — wood and stone split apart.

526It is some days now since Dasa Gadadhara
came from Navadvipa to Kantaka-nagara.56

527Singing the glories of Gora, he moans day and night;
at the sight of that state the chest bursts.

528He speaks incoherently, at one moment falls silent,
at another tells the glories of Gadadhara Pandita,

529at another, crying 'Nityananda!', heaves a deep sigh,
at another says, 'Where has Pandita Srivasa gone?'

530at another says, 'O Prabhu, to make [me] endure this sorrow,
how many more days will You keep [me] on earth?'

531Saying many such things and sighing deeply,
he lies all but lifeless, fallen in the Lord's courtyard.

532He stays in solitude, takes neither food nor water;
in the burning fire of separation his body sways.

533O Srinivasa! The masters in Navadvipa
have, day by day, nearly all withdrawn from sight.

534Words do not come to the lips, the heart breaks:
Devi Vishnupriya has passed from sight."

535Hearing this, Srinivasa Acharya fainted:
his body motionless, his nostrils without breath.

536Seeing Srinivasa's state, all the Vaishnavas
were distraught; their chests were flooded with tears.

537Only late in the night did the Acharya regain outer consciousness;
he weeps so that stone would split.

538A certain worthy man named Sri Gopala Dasa,
taking Srinivasa in his arms, consoles him at length.

539After some time Srinivasa Acharya grew calm;
the night was nearly over in the kirtana of the Lord.

540Everyone lay down for a little while;
the goddess of sleep drew Srinivasa to herself.

541In the guise of a dream, Prabhu Sri Advaita, full of prema,
appeared in person — His form conquers Kandarpa.57

542His two charming eyes reach to His ears;
His beautiful face puts millions of moons to shame.

543With His arms, which surpass golden lotus stalks,
He lovingly took hold of Srinivasa and held him to Himself.

544Whatever brings relief from the burning fire of separation —
that the merciful Sri Advaita did.

545Showing much fatherly affection, in sweet and gentle words,
smiling softly, He speaks to Srinivasa:

546"Through you many souls will be delivered;
you will preach the Prabhu's teaching everywhere.

547The wise will tell you to marry;
you shall marry — do not grieve over it in your heart."

548Having said many such things, the Prabhu vanished;
Srinivasa, waking, sees that the night has given way to dawn.

549Thinking of the lovely ways of Prabhu Advaita,
he cannot hold back his tears; his heart overflows.

550Consoling himself, in the morning, having finished his morning duties,
Srinivasa went quickly to Shrikhanda.

551Entering Shrikhanda with joy in his heart,
he went to the courtyard of Gauranga and beholds Gaurachand.58

552Rolling on the ground, he offered many obeisances;
his golden body turned grey with dust.

553Hearing that Srinivasa had come, Sri Raghunandana
went before Thakura and told him.

554Although Sri Thakura's heart was burnt with sorrow,
still he became joyful on hearing this.

555He says to Sri Raghunandana in the sweetest words,
"Let my eyes be soothed — bring [him]; let me see Srinivasa."

556Hearing Thakura's words, with a joyful heart
he goes and meets Srinivasa in the Lord's courtyard.

557Sri Raghunandana, a great treasury of virtues,
on finding Srinivasa felt as if he had found life.

558When Srinivasa bowed to Sri Raghunandana,
he embraced him and would not let him go from his arms.

559With what wondrous affection his heart overflows!
Embracing [him], he cannot stop the streams from his eyes.

560Srinivasa floats in the tears of both his eyes;
like one helpless, he stays in Raghunandana's embrace.

561Sri Raghunandana, having bathed him in the tears of his eyes,
took him to where Sri Thakura Narahari was.

562He is sitting in complete seclusion;
at that sight Srinivasa lost his composure.

563Ah! That very form which gladdens the heart —
can a golden champaka be any comparison for it?

564Such an incomparable form has grown wan;
the most tender body wastes away moment by moment.

565The sweetness of his face was like the beauty of the moon;
now it is like a lotus without water.

566Those eyes that showered bliss —
in those eyes there are now constant, abundant streams of tears.

567Gazing and gazing at such Narahari Prabhu,
he bows to the ground, intoxicated with the rasa of bhakti.

568Sri Thakura Narahari, seeing him, in a surge of affection
said, "Come, my son!" and embraced Srinivasa.

569Embracing Srinivasa, he was overwhelmed;
he cannot hold back the tears of both his eyes.

570He bathed Srinivasa in tears of prema
and, taking him by the hand, seated him by his side.

571With the deepest fatherly affection he strokes his body with his hand;
seeing that wondrous way, who would not be happy?

572Whatever he asks in the sweetest words,
Srinivasa relates it all in order.

573He related everything that had happened from beginning to end
and told him that Narottama had gone to Kshetra.

574What arose in his heart on hearing all this —
does anyone else have the power to tell it?

575Again he says to Srinivasa with affectionate words:
"I greatly long to see Narottama soon.

576I believe Narottama will come here quickly;
many works will be accomplished through him.

577With him you will be intoxicated in sankirtana
and find relief from the burning of cruel separation.

578O my son, it is good that you came quickly:
at this time I have looked at you to my eyes' content.

579Live long and earn bhakti;
distribute the books of bhakti everywhere.

580People will become self-willed, abandoning their own dharma;
they will not understand the inner truth of guru, Krishna and the Vaishnavas.

581These unbelievers you will deliver by the power of bhakti;
all the Vaishnavas will sing your glory.

582You are an eternal servant of Krishna-Chaitanyachandra;
the Lord will fulfil your desire.

583Your mother is a supreme Vaishnavi;
stay for some days in Yajigrama, serving her.

584Whatever her heart desires must certainly be done;
in this there will be no loss for you.

585Marry, my son — this is my wish."
Having said this, he speaks again to Sri Raghunandana:

586"I tell him to marry — how does it seem to you?"
Hearing this, he says, "This is in the minds of all of us."

587Thakura says, "Do not delay in this."
Hearing it, Srinivasa felt great embarrassment.

588Sri Thakura Narahari knows all truths;
saying many things to him, he dispelled his shyness and the rest.

589The Acharya understood that such was Thakura's wish
and reflected on the command Prabhu Advaita had given him in a dream.59

590Breaking his silence, he says, "I cannot transgress the command."
At the Acharya's words joy arose in everyone.

591Sri Thakura Narahari, with gentle words,
gave beloved Srinivasa leave to go to Yajigrama.

592Sri Raghunandana, holding Srinivasa's hand,
slowly came to the Lord's courtyard.

593With all the Vaishnavas living in Shrikhanda
Srinivasa met in the Lord's courtyard.

594Staying there a while and taking leave,
he went quickly from Khanda to Yajigrama.

595Staying there a while, he could not be at peace
and very soon came to Kantaka-nagara.

596In a surge of prema he had darshan of Gauranga;
in Gauranga's courtyard he became grey with dust.

597He went to the secluded place where Gadadhara Dasa was.
What shall I say of how distraught his heart was!

598He has no food, no drink — nothing pleases him;
grey with dust, he constantly rolls on the ground.

599That lovely body, which surpassed a golden lotus,
has grown wan beyond words.

600He has not even half a sesame seed's worth of hope for life;
he sings Gora's virtues, and now and then heaves long sighs.

601Now, remembering Nityananda's virtues and deeds,
taking the name of Advaita, he falls silent.

602Now, taking the name of Gadadhara Pandita,
he speaks piteously, bathed in tears:

603"O Gadadhara! What was in my heart before
did not fall to my lot: you went first, leaving me behind."

604So he says many things that others find hard to understand;
the glory of Gadadhara is known to Gadadhara.60

605What wondrous affection Pandita Sri Gadadhara had for Gadadhara Dasa —
who can describe it?

606Srinivasa, going before such a Gadadhara,
bows to the ground, bathed in tears.

607Prabhu Gadadhara, seeing beloved Srinivasa,
opened his arms and in a surge of affection drew him to his breast.

608With great kindness he says again, softly:
"By the Lord's will I see you again.

609How you went from Gauda to Vrindavana,
how you lived there and studied,

610how Sri Gopala Bhatta gave you the mantra of initiation,
what mercy all the Lord's dear associates showed you,

611how there you met with great love Narottama,
whom the Lord drew to Himself in the village of Ramakeli,

612how you wandered in Vraja with Narottama,
how you set out for Gauda, taking the books,

613how the king of robbers stole the books,
how the books were recovered in Vana-Vishnupur —61

614all this I have heard, my son; what more is there to say?
In my heart is the wish to see Narottama just once.

615O Srinivasa, this is what arises in my heart:
Narottama Dasa will soon come here."

616Having said this and heaving a very long sigh,
he remained silent for some time.

617Who can understand his ways? Again to Srinivasa
he speaks, distressed, in a faltering voice:

618"However you saw things in Navadvipa when you went there —
day by day that ocean of sorrow has grown.

619Srivasa Pandita and the other dear associates of the Lord,
before our very eyes, have almost all withdrawn from sight.

620How Devi Vishnupriya disappeared from view —
it cannot be put into words; the heart breaks.

621Navadvipa has fallen almost into darkness;
all who still remain there are barely alive.

622What shall I say? I came here from there,
and shameless life still stays in this sinful body."

623Hearing this, Srinivasa cannot keep his composure;
both his eyes were flooded with streams of tears.

624After a while Gadadhara Dasa, composing himself,
speaks in a surge of affection, looking at Srinivasa's face:

625"Live long, my son, remaining on earth;
you will make known the inner essence of bhakti together with your own people.62

626The supremely rare sankirtana of Sri Prabhu
you will relish ceaselessly together with your own people.

627You will soon marry, with everyone's consent;
many will become your followers."

628Saying many such things, he kindly
gave Srinivasa leave to go to his mother.

629Srinivasa took his leave and went home,
and increased his mother's supreme joy.

630Writing a letter with the news, he quickly
sent it by a messenger to Vana-Vishnupur.

631In Yajigrama he lives happily with his disciples
and has them study the books of the Gosvamis.

632Just as the Gosvamis revealed the doctrine that is best of all,
so Acharya Srinivasa expounds it.

633Adherents of false doctrines, hearing his exposition of bhakti,
flee far away, like dogs in fear of a lion.

634Hosts of learned men, knowing bhakti to be supreme,
come to Srinivasa's feet and beg for shelter.

635Whoever feels joy on hearing all this —
to him Gaurachandra, together with His associates, shows mercy.

636Whoever always recites this to people endowed with faith
sinks into the ocean of the rasa of bhakti for Krishna.

637Meditating on the feet of Srinivasa Acharya,
Narahari Dasa tells the Bhakti-ratnakara.

Thus in the Sri Bhakti-ratnakara ends the seventh wave, called "The Description of the Spreading of the Books of Bhakti and Other Matters".
